# Cairn

> A federated search engine for open data and machine learning — one query across Hugging Face, arXiv, GitHub, Zenodo, data.gov, OpenML and Kaggle, streaming results live and ranking every one with a transparent Reproducibility Score.

## About

Cairn is a federated search engine for the open research ecosystem. A single query is fanned out across seven independent providers in parallel, and datasets, papers, models and code stream back live as they arrive. Results are deduplicated across sources, ranked by a transparent reproducibility signal, and every card ships with the exact code to load or download what you found.

## Key facts

- No API keys or sign-up required for basic search. Optional AI features run on a free Groq tier.
- Seven sources: Hugging Face (datasets & models), arXiv (papers), GitHub (code repositories), Zenodo (datasets), data.gov (government datasets), OpenML (ML datasets), Kaggle (datasets & notebooks).
- Results stream live over server-sent events (SSE) as each provider responds; a slow or failing source never blocks the others.
- Every result carries a transparent 0-100 Reproducibility Score: 20% metadata, 20% license, 35% liveness (page reachable?), 25% maintenance (recently updated?).
- Optional Discuss mode expands natural-language queries into related search terms via Groq; expansions are cached 7 days and fall back silently to the exact query on any failure.
- Optional AI Insight produces a one-click plain-language summary per result; cached 21 days, rate-limited daily.
- Provider responses are cached in a zero-infrastructure SQLite file (2-hour TTL) with a small in-memory LRU on top.
- Searches are anonymous: no accounts, no analytics, no server-side query logs. Nothing is re-hosted — every result links to the original provider.
- Optional personal Kaggle credentials are AES-256-GCM encrypted on-device and only ever sent to Kaggle for the user's own search.
